If one is unable to perform the fire-sacrifice (homakarma), one should perform double the recitation;
having recited one hundred and eight times, the preceptor should then employ the rosary.
Then, having himself recited it one hundred and eight times over the hand of the disciple,
he should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the guru according to his means.
[The time for the self-consecration of the rosary: In the absence of a guru, one should perform the consecration of the rosary oneself.
[Daily recitation with the rosary at the end of worship: One should perform the recitation with the rosary daily at the conclusion of the worship.
One should first sprinkle the rosary with water and recite the mantra over it, and likewise do so at the conclusion of the worship.
[The specific mantra for the garland worship:

Having uttered the Vāgbhava-bīja, the Bhuvaneśvarī-mantra, the Akṣamālā-mantra, and the Ṣoḍaśākṣarī-mantra, as well as the Hṛdaya-mantra, the most excellent practitioner should perform the worship. (150)
[The Mantra for Requesting the Rosary] Oṃ, O rosary, O rosary, O great rosary, you whose nature is all powers!
The four aims of life have been entrusted to you; therefore, be the bestower of success upon me. (151)
[The Consecration of the Garland] Having consecrated it, one should then take the garland in the right hand;
the mantra is said to end with the heart-mantra, preceded by *māyā* (the syllable *hrīṃ*) and ending in *siddheśvarī ṇentā*. || 152 ||
150. "Vāgbhava," etc. By this, the mantra *aiṃ drīṃ akṣamālāyai namaḥ* is formed. 152. "Having consecrated," etc. By this, the mantra *hrīṃ siddheśvaryai namaḥ* is accomplished.
This five-syllabled mantra is used during the ritual of seizing [the power] and at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*).
Having brought [it] to the region of the heart, one should not, however, touch it with the left hand.
[The rule for finger placement during the recitation with a rosary:
Having placed [the rosary] on the middle part of the middle finger, being composed, one should not touch the rosary with the index finger, and one should move it with the tip of the thumb. 154.
Taking each seed individually, one should not even cross over Mount Meru;
for the highest rite, one should recite with the thumb and ring finger,
while for the rites of inciting hatred and expulsion, the recitation is performed with the combination of the index finger and the thumb.
One should perform the recitation for the rite of killing by joining the little finger and the thumb. [The placement of the rosary at the end of the recitation:
At the conclusion of the recitation, having placed the rosary upon one's head, one should worship it with this [mantra]. || 156 ||
O Mālā, you who always grant pleasure to all the gods, bestow auspiciousness upon me, O blessed one, as well as fame and valor at all times. (157)
[The Concealment of the Garland]:
At the conclusion of the recitation, the wise and disciplined practitioner should carefully conceal that garland;
even during the time of recitation, the beautiful rosary must be kept hidden. 158.
[The Prohibition of Recitation Without Counting:
"If one performs recitation while transgressing the rules for counting, the Rākṣasas seize that recitation; therefore, a wise person should count in every way. (159)
157 | "O Mālā! This mantra is found in another tantra:
"O Mālā, you are considered the bestower of all accomplishments (*siddhi*) for all the gods.
By that truth, O Mother, grant me accomplishment; salutations to you. Thus it is said.
159. Regarding "counting" (*gaṇanā*): the necessity of counting has been stated. This is also the authority in the *Tantrasāra*. Furthermore, in the *Viśvasāra* as cited in the *Tantrasāra* (p.
788), concerning the time for stringing the beads of the rosary:
When the thread has worn out, one should string a new thread and recite the mantra one hundred times. [Instruction on what must be done when the rosary suffers defects such as falling from the hand:
If it falls from the hand while making a sound, one should recite it one hundred and eight times. (160)
Likewise, if one touches something forbidden, the knower of mantras should rinse [the hands] and recite [the mantra].
[Another Way of Explaining the Accomplishment of Mantras] Now I shall further explain another supreme method for accomplishing mantras.
[Explaining the Unity of the Mantra and the Practitioner]
The unity of mantra and sādhana is difficult for humans on earth to attain. || 162 ||
It was stated in the Saṃkarṣaṇa Tantra by Śiva, the knower of all, in the past to the wise Śukra, in the Pañcarātra known as Ānanda.

[The Explanation of the Unity of the Disciple and the Mantra: Having given the consecrated and worshipped mantra to the disciple, the teacher should then effect their unity by means of the path seen in the scriptures. (164)
[In that regard, there is a specific rule:
Having interwoven the mantra with the letters of the name in their proper order, one should write the full name at the beginning and the end, and then inscribe the *praṇava* (Oṃ). 165.
The wise person should perform the recitation with a specific count; one should not recite without counting.
For one who acts without counting, everything becomes fruitless.
In the Tantra: Having placed the hand upon the heart and turned the fingers sideways,
covering both hands with a cloth, one should always recite [the mantra] with the right hand.
Regarding the holding of the count of recitations, he states what is prohibited and what is not:
"One should not perform the counting of recitations with unbroken grains (akṣata), nor with the joints of the fingers, nor with grains, nor with flowers, nor with sandalwood, nor with clay."
"Having mixed lac, *kuṣṭha*, vermilion, cow dung, and dried dung, one should form them into pills and perform the recitation according to the prescribed number. (p.
789) "The vowels should be inscribed upon the vessels; one should meditate upon them as being of the nature of nectar."
On a beautiful birch-bark leaf, in the center of a lotus, using yellow pigment (rocana), fragrant substances, and so forth. || 166 ||
Having wrapped that [image] with pure clay and then with beeswax,
one should place it in a small earthen vessel filled with honey.
He should place that small vessel into a new jar filled with milk;
the preceptor should hold the jar near the fire-pit.
Then, for the sake of achieving the unity of the mantra and the practitioner, he should perform the oblation.
The mantra-knower, the practitioner, should pour a thousand or even a hundred oblations of the three auspicious sweet substances into the jar with the root mantra. (169)
Having placed it down, one should cast that jar into great water with the *sana* mantra;
by this sequence, the oneness of the mantra and the practitioner shall indeed be achieved. (170)
[The censure of a teacher who lacks this knowledge: He who does not understand this is not called a teacher. || 171 ||
[Wherever it may be, the secret must not be spoken:
One must not speak of the secret to just anyone once it has been told;
one should speak it only to an excellent disciple or to a beloved son. 172.
[The designation of the "three sweets"]: milk, honey, and ghee in equal measure are known as the "three sweets. || 173 ||

[The secret preliminary rites (*puraścaraṇa*) and so forth are to be known from the *Syāmā-rahasya*: "The secret [rites], the preliminary practices, and the rituals such as the worship of the female messenger (*dūtī-yāga*) are to be understood by the best of practitioners in the *Syāmā-rahasya* according to their terminology. (174)

174. Regarding "the *Rahasya* and so forth": the preliminary practice (*puraścaraṇa*) for the *Rahasya* should be understood from the fifth chapter of the *Syāmā-rahasya*. Furthermore, the ritual procedure for the sacrifice to the female messenger (*dūtī-yāga-vidhi*) is found in the *Syāmā-rahasya* and the *Śrī-krama* (p.
790): "When one-third of the night has passed, a man who has gone to the house of a *Kula* woman..."
With his mouth filled with betel-leaf and fragrant with the scent of incense, he [remained].
His limbs smeared with red sandalwood, anointed with red unguents,
and clothed in red garments, he stands in a house reddened by lac;
enveloped in a red garland and adorned with red flowers.
One should worship the Mistress of the Kula with the conventions of the fivefold process (pañcīkaraṇa).

The characteristics of the leaders of the families are stated in that very same [text]: "The actress, the skull-bearer, the courtesan, the Pukkasi, the barber’s wife, the washerwoman, the dyer, and the eloquent servant-woman."
Khaṭikā, Ghaṭikā, and likewise Gopālakanyakā—
all these noble women were endowed with exceptional cleverness.
Devoted to the guru and devoted to the gods, yet devoid of compassion and shame,
and generally delighting in concealment, young women grant all spiritual accomplishments.
Thus, having established [the image] upon a cushion of flowers as described, one should begin the worship.
It is said in that very same place:
"One who is perfected in the practice of non-duality, free from aversion and shame,
devoted to virtuous conduct, of a sattvic nature, and endowed with devotion."
One who is endowed with the nature of a deity, devoted to the guru, firm in her vows,
free from envy and laziness, compassionate, and affectionate toward her devotees.
Endowed with qualities such as cleverness, magnanimity, courtesy, and compassion;
perfected in beauty and youth; and rich in virtuous conduct and good fortune.
Whether she has been constantly attended to, or has arrived by appointment,
or has come at that very moment, tormented by the fire of passion.
Anointed with red perfume, adorned with red garments,
bound with fragrant flowers, and decorated with all kinds of ornaments.
One should employ that slender woman, who has been well-perfumed with incense, in the work of a messenger;
and one should worship her, in such a state, upon a couch of flowers.

And so forth. Since this is specifically delineated in the *Syāmārahasya* in the ninth chapter, one should consult that very source. It has not been written here in its entirety for fear of prolixity.
(p. 791) [The Description of the Offering of the Bali Sacrifice]
Now, therefore, I shall describe the offering of the bali-oblation which is dear to Śrī;
first uttering the Praṇava, one should then recite the pair of words "Padme. (175)
One should utter "mahāpadme" as the first word, followed by "padmāvati";
thereafter, ending with the wife of fire (svāhā), one should offer the bali-oblation at a crossroads.
One should utter the Praṇava, then the word "Bhuvaneśānī," followed by "Ekajaṭe"; one should speak the term "Mahāyakṣmādhipam" and then extract the word "Tāraya. (177)
One should say to Mamopanītaka: "Accept the offering; take my two steps;
cause my pair of yokes to be taken; grant me the peace of all things. (178)
Having divided the *paravidyā* into two parts, one should join it with the *truṭi*-pair;
then, having added the *māyābīja* and *huṃ*, one should offer the *bali* at nightfall.
Two bali-mantras have been proclaimed for the sake of the spiritual accomplishments (siddhi) desired by heroes. || 180 ||
Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the *Śrītattvacintāmaṇi* composed by the venerable Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. 20.

175–76 | As for the mantra for the offering of the *bali*: *oṃ padme padme mahāpadme padmāvati svāhā*. With this, one should offer the *bali* at a crossroads. 177–80 | Regarding "the syllable *praṇava*" and so forth: the second mantra is—*oṃ hrīḥ ekajaṭe mahāyakṣmādhipaṃ tāraya*.
"Accept, accept the offering brought to me! Cause it to be accepted! Grant me complete peace, grant it!

Having drawn forth the spells of others again and again, shatter them, shatter them! Cut them, cut them! Hrīḥ! Huḥ! Thus, these two offering mantras have been taught here for the sake of the accomplishment of those who follow the conduct of heroes (vīrācārin).
The Twenty-first Chapter:
[An Exposition of Expiations for Killing a Brahmin and Other Sins] Now I shall declare the expiations for the faults of killing a Brahmin and other such offenses. (1)
[In that regard, the sequence is as follows:
One should worship the wheel, which is endowed with all its rays, using red flowers;
it should be adorned with camphor powder according to the very sequence of the family tradition (kulācāra). || 2 ||
[Regarding the restriction of time:
Within three months, all the millions of great sins committed in previous lives are certainly destroyed in an instant.
Lakṣmī is under his control in his house, firmly established and granting all desires. || 3 ||
[The Praise of Worship with Javā Flowers] The knower of mantras should worship Śivā with javā flowers as before;
[thereby] even sins such as the killing of a Brahmin committed in previous births [are purified].
He shall destroy [all sins]; of this there is no doubt; the man becomes wealthy. || 4 ||
[The fruit of worship with fragrant flowers:
One should constantly worship Śivā even with fragrant flowers;
one whose soul is burdened by great sins shall become a destroyer of sin at that very moment. || 5 ||

[The Fruit of Worship with Śamī and Other Materials: Furthermore, by means of śamī wood, dūrvā sprouts, and aśvattha shoots, the practitioner destroys within one month the impurity committed throughout seven lifetimes. (6)
p. 793) [The Fruit of Worship with Ketakī Leaves]:
If one worships as before with fresh leaves of the *ketakī* tree, one shall destroy the multitude of minor offenses (*upapātaka*); there is no doubt in this matter.
Incomparable and most wonderful good fortune arises for him.
[The fruit of worship with hundred-petaled lotuses: Through worship with hundred-petaled lotuses, one shall destroy all evil. [The fruit of worship with white lotuses:]
Sin committed in previous births [is destroyed] by worshipping with white lotuses. || 8 ||
By following the very sequence of family tradition, one becomes the beloved of Saubhāgyā;
by worshipping with white lotuses, one purifies the sins committed in twenty lifetimes.
Within a single month, liberation stands within the grasp of him and his entire lineage.
[The fruit of worship with Bandhūka flowers:
If one should worship in every way with pure bandhūka flowers, the three worlds will surely come under his control, and he will certainly remove all evil. 10.

[The fruit of worship with bilva leaves and lotuses: By worshipping together with both bilva leaves and aquatic flowers, one becomes prosperous and likewise becomes the remover of all sins oneself. (11)
[The fruit of worship with jasmine and other flowers:
One should worship for the duration of one month with jasmine, *mālatī*, *jātī*, *kunda*, and *śatapatraka* flowers, as well as pure white lotuses. (12)
Even the sin committed over twenty lifetimes is [removed] by worshipping with *campaka* flowers;
likewise, the transgression born of a hundred lifetimes is removed through the very sequence of family tradition.
It destroys [the sin] produced by killing a Brahmin and so forth; there is no doubt in this matter.
Liberation is surely in his hand, and by his word he is equal to Brahma on earth. (14)
[The fruit of worship with Agastya and other flowers: By means of the Agastya, Bāṇa, Bandhūka, Javā, and red lotuses as well, one likewise destroys sin and becomes equal to Kāma himself. || 15 ||

[The fruit of worship with *campaka* and other flowers: If the practitioner should worship with *campaka*, *pāṭala*, *vakula*, *nāgakeśara*, *kahlāra*, and *sindhuvāra* flowers, [he shall obtain the desired result].
Indeed, within just one month, his good fortune shall become incomparable.
[The Explanation of the Ritual for Jewel Worship] Now I shall explain specifically the ritual for the worship of jewels. || 17 ||
The practitioner of mantra should fashion flowers made of rubies;
with these, the worship of the King of Mandalas (cakrarāja) should be performed as before, using various fragrant flowers smeared with powdered camphor. (18)
[The fruit of worship with precious flowers and so forth:
Within twenty-one nights, twenty lords of the earth shall indeed become one's servants, and one shall destroy great diseases. (19)
The practitioner becomes as radiant as the sun; of this there is no doubt. || 20 ||
15–16 | *Agastya* etc. *Agastya* is the *vaku* flower; *bāṇā* is the blue *jhiṇṭī*. As Amara states: "The blue *jhiṇṭī* is called *bāṇā*, *dāsī*, and *ārtagala*.
*Bandhūka* is the *bandhujīvaka* (known as *dupahariyā*). As Amara states: "*Bandhūka* is the *bandhujīvaka*."
The *pāṭala* is the flower of the *pāṭalā* tree (some say it is the flower known as *golāba*). (p.
795) Those golden flowers which are marked with pearl-jewels—with those, as well as with various other jewels, worship should be performed as before. || 21 ||
Within twenty-one nights, the wives of kings become submissive; the practitioner becomes endowed with artistic grace and beauty, and is born as a fortunate man upon the earth. (22)
[The fruit of worship with coral and golden flowers:
One should worship with many flowers made of coral and gold, as well as with various other kinds of flowers, for seven days according to the family tradition. (23)
All cruel factions will come under his control, and he shall destroy the ranks of his enemies.
Likewise, by offering *marataka* flowers, the fruit of worship is that one's enemy will certainly become a friend. (24)
[The fruit of worship with ruby flowers: One should worship the Maṇḍala with flowers made of great rubies (*padmarāga*) combined with gold,
proceeding in sequence for three weeks.
All the Suras are under his control, and he shall become equal to Bṛhaspati. || 25 ||
[The fruit of worship with gold flowers set with diamonds:
With flowers fashioned from gold and scented with diamond-encrusted ketakī blossoms, one may enchant this entire world within twenty-one nights. 26.
Gods and Daityas alike become subject to his will; of this there is no doubt. || 27 ||
[The fruit of worship with golden flowers set with sapphire gems:
One should worship the Discus with golden flowers made of sapphires;
likewise, for twenty-one nights, one should worship it with blue lotuses.
Enemies meet their destruction, and the rest become submissive. || 28 ||

[The fruit of worship with gold flowers set with gomedaka: With gold flowers set with *gomedaka*, with *kunda* and *kiṃśuka* flowers, an enemy becomes submissive within seven days; their destruction occurs among them.
Within three weeks, one will certainly destroy the accumulation of great sins. || 29 ||
[The fruit of worship with flowers made of new gold and jewels:
One should also worship with fresh flowers made of gold and jewels;
then, the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices is certainly obtained. || 30 ||
Those who live as meat-eaters will indeed become submissive; of this there is no doubt.
[The fruit of worship with gold flowers set with lapis lazuli:
With gold flowers fashioned from lapis lazuli, such as campaka and jasmine blossoms, [the fruit of worship is attained].
Having worshipped the Cakrarāja, one may paralyze the three worlds in an instant.
After twenty-one recitations, it shall become a destroyer of great sins. || 32 ||
[The fruit of worship with golden flowers set with various jewels:
If one should worship Śivā with golden flowers composed of various jewels, then the gods, sages, serpents, rākṣasas, and others [shall be pleased]. || 33 ||
All indeed become submissive within three weeks; of this there is no doubt.
It shall destroy the sins of the practitioner accumulated over ten million births. 34.
[The fruit of worship with flowers containing even a small amount of gold, jewels, and so forth:
Furthermore, even if one does not possess an abundance of gold, jewels, and the like, the worship must indeed be performed by the best of practitioners using those very same flowers. (35)
One should worship the Mistress of the Wheel with the very nature of ornaments;
indeed, with mere flowers, one may paralyze the three worlds. (36)
Within a single month, one shall destroy the sins accumulated over seven lifetimes and delude the entire earth encircled by the oceans. (37)
[Prohibition of worship with stale flowers:

One should not worship even with flowers made of gold if they are stale. [Prohibition of worship with flowers that have already been offered: One should not worship with flowers that have already been offered (nirmālya).
One should not worship with flowers that have become faded or with those that are defiled by food remnants. || 38 ||
[The fruit of worship with leaves such as Apāmārga:
One should diligently worship the Supreme Goddess with these leaves: Apāmārga, Bhṛṅga, Bilva, and even Marakata. (39)
[The Description of Śākta Flowers: By means of the ambhoja, utpala, bandhujīva, vijayā, punnāga, nāga, ujjātī, kunda, kuraṇṭa, campaka, javā, yūthī, ramā, and pāṭala flowers;
Flowers from the bilva, aśoka, hayāri, kubja, madana, mandāra, dūrvā sprouts, droṇa, agastya, and aparājitā are fully suitable for use with the Śakti. (40)
[One should perform worship with jasmine, tagara, and so forth.
With flowers produced at all times, such as jasmine, tagara, and others—whether white or red—one should diligently worship the Supreme Goddess. (41)

40 | *Ambhojotpala* etc.: *Vijayā* is *śephālikā*; *punnāga* is the *keśara* flower; *nāga* is the *nāgakeśara* flower; *kuraṇṭa* is the red *jhiṇṭī* flower; *hayāri* is the *karavīra* flower; *kubja* is the fruit of *apāmārga*; *madana* is the *vakula* flower (or known as *mayanā*); *mandāra* is the *arka* flower (known as *ākanda*).
p. 798) [Prohibition of worship with buds:
Likewise, worship is not desired with buds, except for those of the *campaka* and the lotus.
[Absence of the fault of stale flowers regarding the lotus and the *campaka*: ]
There is no fault of being stale in the case of the water-born lotus or the campaka flower either. || 42 ||
[Description of the Yantra-Flowers:
In this regard, there is the Aparājita flower, the excellent flower called Javā, as well as the white and red Karavīra flowers, and indeed the Droṇā flower. (43)
The Goddess should always reside within these; one should worship her in that yantra.
Therefore, the practitioner of mantra should diligently honor her with these flowers. 44.
In the *Yoginītantra*, in the section on Tripurā:
[Certain injunctions and prohibitions regarding specific flowers]—One should avoid the *śephālikā* and the *kahlāra* except during the autumn season. (45)
O Maheśvarī, one should worship the Bakula, Aśoka, and Arjuna flowers with their stalks; however, one should avoid [using] the stalk of the Bakula.
One should worship Viṣṇukrāntā, Javā, Nāgakeśara, Nāgavallabha, Bandhūka, and Kahlāra together with their stalks.
One should not touch [the flowers] except at their stalks, nor should one touch them while they remain on the ground;
one should treat the śephālī and the vakula in the same manner as those that have fallen to the earth.
Having placed flowers together with unbroken rice (akṣata) and likewise smeared with red [pigment],
and having finally positioned Sundarī, one should likewise place a red flower.
[The Excellence of the Bilva Leaf] Having diligently offered bilva leaves to the Goddess among all leaves,
a worship performed without bilva leaves is seen to be of no avail in either the Śākta or the Śaiva traditions. (50)
[The excellence of vermilion on the stage of the body:
Vermilion is supremely pleasing to the Goddess on the stages of the limbs;
therefore, the practitioner should diligently offer vermilion.
[The excellence of betel among mouth-fresheners:
Among mouth-fresheners, betel is the supreme bringer of joy to the Goddess. (51)
If one worships Pārvatī according to this very procedure, one obtains one's desired object within seven nights; there is no doubt about this. || 52 ||
[The excellence of specific flowers on specific days of the week: On Sunday, with red lotuses; on Monday, with night-lilies (kumuda);
on Tuesday, with red water-lilies (raktotpala); on Wednesday, with those produced from tagara. || 53 ||
One should worship with white lilies on Thursdays, with white lotuses on Fridays,
and with blue lotuses on Saturdays, for a year, with devotion.
[Substances to be offered on specific days of the week: One should offer these in sequence on those seven days beginning with Sunday:
milk-rice, milk, plantain, fresh butter, sugar, and ghee. (55)
[The Fruit of Worshipping the Goddess for One Year] Having propitiated the Goddess for one year in due order with perfumes and other offerings,
one quickly overcomes the afflictions of the planets and enjoys all forms of happiness. (56)
55. "One should offer" means: *sitā* is sugar.
(p. 800) [The fruit of worshipping the Goddess on a mountain peak:
One should worship the Goddess at night on a mountain peak with *palāśa* flowers.
And by means of perfected substances, the union with the Khecarī occurs within seven days. || 57 ||
[The Fruit of Worship in Forests and Other Places:
In a forest, at the foot of a banyan tree, or in a grove among mountains,
one should worship Śivā with *kadamba* and *jāti* flowers and with consecrated substances.
Within a month, the accomplished ḍākinīs become manifest, bestowing all that is desired. || 58 ||

[The Fruit of Worship on the Seashore] By means of *ketakī* flowers, the Siddhas and *ceṭakas* on the shore of the ocean [attain] their desired command, a woman, desire, and the most wonderful illusion (*māyā*).
They should abundantly give him wealth, garlands, and ornaments according to his desire. || 59 ||
[The Fruit of Worshipping the Goddess upon a Seat of Akṣa Trees:
Having constructed a seat from akṣa trees, one should worship the Goddess there at night with śālmalī flowers and consecrated substances for a month, remaining fearless. (60)
[The fruit of worship in the cremation ground:
In the land of the ancestors, the lord of practitioners attains accomplishment; [the danger regarding the attainment of a vetāla: the piśācīs [become his servants].
For one month, he remained fearless in a solitary forest during the night. || 61 ||
One should worship the Goddess situated within the wheel, accompanied by the substances of accomplishment,
with *mālatī*, *jāti*, *punnāga*, *ketakī*, and honey, in due order.
60. "The seat is made of *akṣa*": that is, with *vibhītaka* trees.
By means of that, the *vetālas* are accomplished, and then one may move about according to one's own will.
[The fruit of worshipping the Goddess at a specific place at midnight.]
In a cremation ground, in the temple of Caṇḍikā, or in a solitary forest; || 63 ||
At midnight, adorned with black garments and other ornaments, one should worship the Goddess;
having saluted that exceedingly dark goddess within the black circle, one should perform her full adoration.
Then, before that, one should offer a sacrificial oblation (bali) consisting of the materials for accomplishment,
accompanied by the substances of success, after observing the signs of that state for a month.
From them are born terrifying black [beings];
one should offer what is to be accomplished to them, who are pleased by the destruction of the universe and who return again by their own will.
[The obstacle to the perfection of the power of concealment:
Through the prayer of the Goddess, [the obstacles] become concealed within her forehead-eye. 67.
[The Means for Great Accomplishment:
Adorned with red ornaments and garments, his body decorated with a garland of human heads, he should meditate upon the Goddess in a secluded grove and worship her. 68.
With white water-lilies, campaka flowers, aśoka, pāṭala, and śatapatra flowers,
combined with the substances of the perfected ones, magical powers (māyās) are accomplished within a month.
[The Means for Accomplishing the Power of Desire and Form] By attaining serenity for one month, a man becomes one who can take any form at will;
by means of these [powers], he became a wanderer through the universe, possessing universal sport. 70.
p. 802) [The Means for Accomplishing Knowledge of the Three Times] One should meditate upon and worship the wheel in the center of the six supports (ādhāra),
using substances produced from camphor, sandalwood, musk, and the secretions of the musk deer.
One who knows the three times should contemplate the Goddess thoroughly within them.
[The Fruit of Worshipping the Goddess in a Betel Grove] One should worship the Goddess day and night with consecrated substances in a betel grove;
by dwelling there and using those flowers, one becomes like the God of Love. (72)
[The fruit of worshipping the Goddess during the full moon at a Kanyā festival:
One should certainly worship the Goddess during the full moon at a Kanyā festival;
the spells (kṛtyās) sent by enemies and the mantras become turned away and indeed devour them. 73.
[The Discourse on the Installation of Madana] I shall describe the installation of Madana for the benefit of practitioners,
by means of which the worship performed throughout the year reaches its fulfillment. (74)
Formerly, because he was the cause of the interruption of Śiva’s asceticism, Madana was reduced to ashes; at that time, his wives Rati and Prīti were deeply distressed. (75)
At that time, from the water produced by his eyes, there arose the flower of Madana;
its fragrance and its great beauty were truly wonderful. (76)
With a heart satisfied by that, Śiva granted a boon;
therefore, Madana was restored to his natural state for the sake of Rati and Prīti.
And whatever mantra-practitioner worships Madana during the course of a year, his worship for that entire year will be directed toward Madana. (78)
71 | Regarding "the six supports" (*ṣaḍādhāra*): "moon" (*candra*) refers to camphor (*karpūra*).
73 | Regarding "on the full [moons]" (*pūrṇāsu*): on the full-moon days (*pūrṇimāsu*). (p.
803) Thus was a boon granted to her by the high-souled Śaṅkara.
Therefore, the worship of Madana must be performed by the best of practitioners. || 79 ||
One should worship Madana either with its roots or with its clusters;
one should divide Madana into nine parts and worship it immediately thereafter.
One should worship Madana in sequence with the seed-syllable of Ānandeśvara, nine times along with the Bindu, differentiated in various ways.
One should indeed consecrate that very person with the mantra known as Aghora:
Māyā, Sphurad-dvaya, Bhūyas, Prasphurad-dvitaya, and again [Māyā]. (82)
One should write the word *tvarūpa* after the [mantras] that are most terrible (*ghoraghoratara*). At the end of those, one should again write two *caṭa*s and two *prakaṭa*s.
The mantra of Ghoraka consists of the pair *kaha*, the pair *vaśa*, then the words *bandha bandha*, followed by the pair *ghātaya*, and ends with the armor (*varma*) and *phaṭ*. (84)

This is the Vāgbhava [seed-syllable]: Śiva (Ś) and Candra (C), ending with Mādana (M), followed by Pānta (P) conjoined with Vahni (R), pierced by Śakti (I), and enriched with Bindu, Nāda, and Kalā. (85)
81–84 | Regarding "Ānandeśvara": the mantra of Ānandabhairava is *hasakṣamalavarayū ānandabhairavāya vaṣaṭ* (as stated in the *Prāṇatoṣaṇī*).
[The mantra] called Aghora is *aghorebhyo 'tha ghorebhyaḥ*, etc. (see page 785).

"Mayā" and so forth. As for the extraction of the mantra: *hrīḥ sphura sphura prasphura prasphura ghora ghoratarebhyaḥ tava rūpaṃ caṭa caṭa prakaṭa prakaṭa kaha kaha vaśa vaśa bandha bandha ghātaya ghātaya huṃ phaṭ*. Thus it is said.
Śiva and Śakti, with Māma and Aśakra, adorned by Vahni and the left eye, and pervaded by Bindu, Nāda, and Kalā—this is the great Kāmarāja. (86)
The seed-syllable of Sadāśiva is indeed the southern [direction], which is exceedingly Bhairavī;
by means of this Śara-mantra and the Kavaca, there is protection.
Having bound the trident mudrā, one should whirl it above the madana.
Having bound the little finger with the thumb and extending the remaining three fingers, this is proclaimed as the Trishula Mudrā (the Trident Gesture). || 89 ||
[The Time for the Installation of Madana: On the fourteenth day of the month of Caitra, the installation of Madana shall take place. [The Procedure for the Installation of Madana:]
One should extract it with the Astra-mantra and dissolve it with the Hṛdaya-mantra. || 90 ||

85. "Śiva-candra-ādi" and so forth: Śiva is the letter *ha*, Candra is the letter *sa*, Mādana is the letter *ka*, the end of *pā* is the letter *pha*, Vahni is the letter *ra*, and Śakti is the letter *e*. By these [letters]...
The mantra is "ha sa ka phre.
86. Regarding the passage beginning with "Śiva and Śakti": Śiva is the letter *ha*, Śakti is the letter *e*, Kāma is the letter *ka*, and Śakra is the letter *la*.
The letter *va* (vahnīraka) is the syllable *ha*, and the left eye (*vāmākṣi*) is the syllable *rī*. Thus, the mantra becomes *ha e ka la rīṃ*.
87. Regarding "of Sadāśiva": the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of Sadāśiva is *hau*; the seed-syllable of Dakṣiṇā is *krī*; [and] the seed-syllable of Bhairavī is...

*Hasarai*, *śaramaṇḍaḥ phaṭ*, *kavacaḥ hūṃ*, *tena hauḥ*, *krīḥ*, *hasaraiḥ*, *phaṭ hūṃ*. This is the extraction of the mantra (88–89). Regarding "having bound": having bound the little finger with the thumb, one should extend the index, middle, and ring fingers; this is the manner of the trident mudrā (*triśūla-mudrā*).
[Therein, the consecration with Madana: One should perform the consecration using solid roots of *śrīkhaṇḍa* (sandalwood) and other such substances.
Having performed the daily worship, one should establish it at night with the Vidyā-mantra. (91)
On the first day, one should perform the excellent preliminary consecration (adhivāsana);
or alternatively, for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of a year-long worship, one may perform the immediate consecration (sadyo'dhivāsana).
[The Section on the Worship of Madana] Having completed the daily worship at dawn on the fourteenth day,
one should then fashion a nine-cornered figure with vermilion, making it exceedingly radiant.
Having arranged water-pots filled with gold, gems, and other precious materials, the most excellent preceptor should install either one or all of them, making them beautiful. 94.
To the south, one should prepare a mandala adorned with sprouts and other offerings;
having drawn an Aśoka tree, one should draw a triangular mandala. (95)
[The meditation on Kāma]:
In the center of that, one should worship Kāma, who has the luster of a youth, with red flowers and red garments, in order from left to right. 96.
For the sake of attaining success, one should worship Kāma together with Vasanta—He who is richly adorned with Rati, Prīti, and Viśobhā, and who wields the bow of the five arrows. || 97 ||
[The Kāma-mantra:
Having written Vāgbhava, Bhuvaneśānī, Śrī, and likewise the essence of Kāma, followed by "Kāmāya namaḥ," this is the nine-syllabled Vidyā. (98)
93 | "In the morning" means: having prepared a nine-cornered mandala with vermilion (sindūra).
98 | "The Vāgbhava," etc. The extraction of the mantra is as follows: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ kāmāya namaḥ*. [This is the Ratimantra. (p. 806)
Having uttered the three seed-syllables of desire, one should recite "Kāmayātmane" once; then "Ratye Namaḥ. This eight-syllable Ratividyā is thus proclaimed. (99)
[The mantra of joy:
One should utter "joy" (prīti) in place of "delight" (rati); this is the eight-syllable mantra of joy. || 100 ||
[The arising of Rati and Prīti: Rati and Prīti are fair and dark-complexioned respectively, adorned with jewels;
they hold lotuses and betel leaves in their hands and are decorated with red colors. 101.
The meditation on Kāmadeva is described as being upon his left and right [sides], which serve as ornaments of knowledge and are adorned with garlands of flowers. 102.
[Subsequently, the worship of Spring:
Thereafter, one should worship Spring, who is situated in the midst of a *kadamba* grove, holding a golden vessel filled with nectar in his left hand. 103.
Having worshipped Kāma along with his limbs, one who holds a collection of various flowers in his right hand should then present incense, lamps, and other offerings. 104.
[After the worship of Madana, then the worship of the Goddess, and then the worship of the Kumārīs:
When Kāma has been worshipped during the Madana [rite], he accomplishes all purposes and goals;
having thoroughly worshipped him, one should then worship Mahātripurasundarī. (105)

99. Regarding "the seed-syllables of desire": having uttered the three seed-syllables of desire, one should utter "kāma" again. Thus, the eight-syllable mantra becomes: *klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ ratyai namaḥ*. 100. Regarding "one should say 'prīti' in place of 'rati'": thus, the *prīti*-mantra becomes: *klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ prītyai namaḥ*.
One should worship with flowers produced at that time, with moon-creepers and sandalwood, with fragrant blossoms along with saffron, and even with the juices of various fruits. (106)
Having performed one hundred and eight [recitations], one should then worship a young maiden;
having fully worshipped a married woman, one should worship the circle of the womb (yonimaṇḍala). || 107 ||
[The Worship of Mahādevī and the Full Oblation] Having worshipped Mahādevī, one should perform the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
[The Giving of the Teacher’s Fee Following the Worship of the Brāhmaṇas]
Having also honored the Brahmins, he should bestow the teacher’s fee (gurudakṣiṇā).
[The Fruit of the Installation of Madana:
By this rite, the mantra-practitioner should perform the installation of Madana;
his annual worship shall be fruitful, and not otherwise. (109)
[Special Worship on the Full Moon of Vaiśākha]:
On the full moon day of the month of Vaiśākha, one should worship the Supreme Goddess with golden flowers;
or else, with camphor, musk, sandalwood, and cool water. (110)
[Special Worship on the Full Moon of Jyeṣṭha]:

And on the full moon day of the month of Jyeṣṭha, one should worship the Goddess with fruits produced from plantain, jackfruit, and mango trees, as before, for the attainment of all perfections. (111)
[The Description of the Offering of the Pavitra] I shall now describe the offering of the pavitra for the benefit of practitioners. 112.

107. Regarding the term *suvāsinī*: it means a woman whose husband is living (*pativatnī*). The method for the worship of the *yoni* should be consulted in the seventh section, fourth chapter, of the *Prāṇatoṣaṇī* and other such works.
(p. 808) [The necessity of performing the worship of the *pavitra*]
Worship performed for even a single year certainly becomes fruitful;
therefore, the Pavitra-worship must indeed be performed for the sake of attaining success.

[The Time for the Installation of the Pavitra: Beginning from the sun's entry into Gemini until the transition into Libra, one should perform a most beautiful great worship, especially that of the pavitras. || 114 ||
She should be worshipped on both fortnights; one should perform the Pavitrāropaṇa rite on the fourth, the eighth, the ninth, or the fourteenth day.
[The Special Rite on the Full Moon of Āṣāḍha:
Or, on the full moon day of the month of Āṣāḍha, one should worship Śivā with sacred threads (*pavitra*) made of gold, silver, copper, or of silk. (116)

[The creation of the nine threads: With threads produced from the sacrificial cord, those originating from lotus stalks, those produced from *trasarī* fibers, and those originating from saffron-colored threads. || 117 ||
One should prepare the pavitras for all the Śaktis using auspicious threads made from darbha, muñja, and śaṇa grass, multiplied ninefold and measuring sixteen finger-breadths in length. || 118 ||
Or, it may be nine finger-breadths long and provided with that same number of arrow-knots;
however, for the fire-oblation (homa), one should make a single arrow-knot and worship them in sequence with those [materials].
[Deity worship on the nine threads:
One should worship the moon of the snowy mountains, Agni, Brahmā, the Nāga, Guha, Hari, myself, and all the gods upon the nine threads. (120)

120. Regarding the verse beginning with "prāleya": the meaning is that one should worship these nine—namely, Prāleya, Candramas, Vahni, Brahmā, Nāga, Guha, Hari, Madakṣa, and Sarvadeva—as the nine [deities] within the nine threads.
Having consecrated them with the *śiras-mantra*, one should [bathe them] with auspicious waters while reciting the *hṛdaya-mantra*.
The preceptor, having washed [the vessel], should perform the sprinkling with the Śiva-mantra.
And having fastened it with a cord through the eye, one should bind it with armor,
using yellow pigment (rocanā), saffron, red sandalwood, and sandalwood.
One should cause it to be made most charming and variegated with musk, saffron, and the like, as well as with pure camphor, red ochre, and other pigments. || 123 ||
Having sprinkled them with the root mantra, one should place them upon a ten-cornered diagram. [The Installation of the Collection of Purifiers:
The entire collection of purifiers is worshipped with the six limbs. (124)
Having performed the installation of the water-pot on the preceding day,
[and having performed] the installation of the water-pot on the preceding day itself,
[regarding the number of threads for the purificatory rite].
It is fashioned with one hundred and eight threads by means of the mantra. || 125 ||
[The description of the highest, middling, and lowest according to the gradation of number:
One should know that to be the highest; half of that would be the middling;
half of that again would be the lowest. Thus it is declared to be threefold in sequence. 126.

121-24 | "With the head-mantra," and so forth. Having consecrated [the rosary] with the head-mantra *svāhā*, one should wash it with auspicious water while reciting the heart-mantra *namaḥ*. One should perform the sprinkling with the Śiva-mantra *hauḥ*. Having secured it with the eye-mantra *vauṣaṭ* and having knotted it together with the armor-mantra *huṃ*, one should cause it to be decorated with yellow pigment (*gorocanā*), saffron (*kuṅkuma*), and other substances.
*Ghusṛṇa* is saffron (*kuṅkuma*). Regarding this, the *Hārāvalī* states: "Saffron is *pītakāvera*; *ghusṛṇa* consists of flowers. (p. 810).
Having fashioned the *śaragranthi* and other [knots] measuring ninety-six finger-breadths for the pure root-energies (*mūlaśakti*), one should offer the triad. (127)
[The Ritual of Acceptance and Worship]:

At the time of the ritual of acceptance (adhivāsana), the practitioner, having scattered barley grains and established the vessel for the Goddess filled with gold and other precious materials, [should proceed]. 128.
Having invoked the Goddess into that pitcher, one should worship her with the root mantra using sandalwood,
white water-lilies and other flowers, as well as fruits; one should worship Śivā with cardamom, kakkola, and jasmine.
[The Offering of the Pavitra] Thereafter, having worshipped the sequence [of deities], one should perform the offering of the *pavitra*.
One should offer the *pavitra*s with the *Śrīvidyā* mantra, using the name of the Guru. (130)

One should perform the rite of offering the sacred thread (pavitrāropaṇa) to the three kinds of gurus, to the groups of lunar-day deities (tithinityā), and also to the Nine Goddesses of the Chakras (navacakreśvarī).
In each of all the clusters of rays, preceded by the syllable *Tāra*, one should then offer the purifying thread (*pavitra*) to Kurukullā. (132)
[Producing Satisfaction for the Guru]: A wise person should satisfy the guru according to their means, with golden ornaments, garments, and collections of various jewels. (133)
The best of practitioners should wear that sacred prasāda;
having performed the ancillary fire-oblation (aṅgahoma), he should offer it with the purifying thread (pavitra). || 134 ||
131. "To the gurus" means to the threefold [gurus], who are threefold due to the distinction between the *parama*, the *parāpara*, and the *parameṣṭhin*.
(p. 811) [The worship of the maiden and others:
One should perform the worship of the maiden (*kumārī*), and thereafter the group of married women (*suvāsinī*).
Yoginīs and yogins, as well as Brāhmaṇas and various classes [of beings], must indeed be worshipped by the preeminent practitioner if he desires his own welfare. (135)
[What is to be done on the full moon of Śrāvaṇa:
On the full moon day of the month of Śrāvaṇa, for the complete pacification of all calamities,
one should worship with vermilion, saffron, and the like, as well as with various types of sandalwood and fruits.
One should worship the Supreme Goddess with blue lotuses and white water lilies.
[What is to be done on the full moon of Bhādrapada:
Now, on the full moon day of the month of Bhādrapada, one should worship the Goddess with ketaka flowers, accompanied by an extensive display of various riches. (137)
[What is to be done on the full moon of Āśvina:

Especially during the month of Āśvayuja, one should worship the Goddess beginning from the first lunar day (pratipad) ending with the new moon (darśānta), and continuing until the full moon (paurṇamāsī). || 138 ||
With *japā*, *aparājitā*, *droṇa*, *karavīra*, and beautiful lotuses; with *saugandhika* and *kahlāra* lilies, as well as garments, ornaments, and mirrors. (139)
With fans, pure vermilion, chowries, sandalwood and other [unguents], various kinds of fruits and substances, and various juices and elixirs; || 140 ||
Having performed worship, one should recite the vidyā; one should offer oblations every day, either a hundred or even a thousand times, for the sake of pleasing Tripurā. (141)
By that, the vidyā shall become perfected; through worship, it makes one a king.
Having performed full worship on the seventh, eighth, or ninth lunar day, one will certainly know [the truth]; if one transgresses this, the opposite occurs. (142)
[What is to be done on the full moon of Kārttika:
On the full moon day of the month of Kārttika, one should worship with saffron and other substances;
then, having offered lamps at night, one should perform a fire sacrifice (homa) with clarified butter. 143.
One should place sixteen lamps before the Goddess in sequence with the Vidyā-mantra;
one should place a single lamp before each of the Śaktis in their respective positions.
Alternatively, having made one [mark] in the center of the vessel and nine around it, one should offer [the oblation],
together with flowers, with the root mantra.
[What is to be performed on the full moon of Mārgaśīrṣa:

On the full moon day of the month of Vṛścika, having offered coconut water accompanied by the moon, one should worship for the entire month according to the prescribed rite with cakes made of flour. 146.
[What is to be performed on the full moon of Pauṣa:
On the full moon day of the month of Pauṣa, one should worship with sugar or jaggery for the sake of attaining mastery over the earth, and one should offer cow's milk as an oblation. || 147 ||
[What is to be done on the full moon of Māgha:
On the full moon day of the month of Māgha, one should worship with white sesame seeds as well as others, together with perfumes, food offerings, white flowers, and so forth. || 148 ||
[What is to be performed on the full moon of Phālguna:

On the full moon day of the month of Phālguna, one should worship with campaka flowers made of gold and silver, and with mango blossoms and fragrant flowers, for the attainment of one's desires. (149)
[Instruction on what is to be performed on the full moons of Caitra and other months:
One should perform special worship on the equinoxes, solstices, new moon days, and the beginnings of the Yugas, as well as on those occasions specifically mentioned in the Āgamas. (150)
[The Necessity of Performing the Duties of the Twelve Months]: "One should diligently perform the duties pertaining to the twelve months;
for year after year, the knower of mantras must do so, otherwise he shall become a partaker of sin."
He shall become the food of the Yoginīs; the glorious Tripurā shall become enraged. || 151 ||
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the *Śrī-Tattvacintāmaṇi* composed by the holy Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. || 21 ||

150. Regarding the phrase "at the equinoxes and solstices" (*viṣuvāyane*): it is indicated by the plural number that special worship must be performed on all the following occasions: on the full moon of the Great Equinox (*mahāviṣuva*), the full moon of the Water Equinox (*jalaviṣuva*), the full moon of the Northern Solstice (*uttarāyaṇa*), the full moon of the Southern Solstice (*dakṣiṇāyana*), on the beginnings of the Yugas (*yugādya*) and the Manvantaras (*manvantarādi*), and on the New Moon days (*darśa*) or *amāvāsyā*s.
The Twenty-second Chapter:
[The Discourse on the Jñānadūtī] Now I shall describe the Jñānadūtī, by whom the eternal Brahman is attained.
One should enter the excellent temple, the sacrificial hall known as Prakāśa. || 1 ||

In that Śiva, who consists of gnosis, fashioned by the messenger-goddesses of will, knowledge, and action, and endowed with his own nature, [one should worship] by means of this supreme messenger-goddess.
On a couch adorned with the goals of human life and the Vedas, and further embellished by the knowledge of the Self, the Inner Self, the Supreme Self, and the Knower of the Self; || 3 ||
The meaning of that word is you, the meaning of the word "you"; the combination of these two words is the Reality.
These three meanings of the words reveal Brahman through knowledge.
One should worship the Supreme Goddess there in that most beautiful [image] woven with bands made of this very sūtra; thereby, the fourfold prosperity shall be attained.
Hastinī, Śaṅkhinī, Citriṇī, and likewise Padminī—
all were endowed with every ornament, beautiful, and possessed of lovely eyes.
Vaikharī is to be known as Hastinī, the supreme power (kalā) in its gross state, by which this entire sphere of the cosmic egg is sustained. (7)
By means of the eight groups [of letters], she invariably gives birth to a multitude of world-elephants;
by that same [measure], she is called a "female elephant" (kariṇī), while the middle one is said to be the "conch-bearer" (śaṅkhinī). || 8 ||
7. Vaikharī is the garland of phonemes beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣ*; Śrīdhara [identifies her] as *vidyā*. (p.
815) And Śaṅkhinī is the Greatly Pure One, free from all sins;
she is indeed beloved by all the gods, adorned with splendor and fragrance. 9.
Likewise, the goddess Citriṇī, who resides in the forest, is the middle one, radiant with auspicious planets; she is the creeper and the embodiment of all powers.
The Goddess, composed of Śiva and Śakti, protects the three worlds;
she is the supreme refuge, beholding all those living beings within them. 10.
Thus merged in Brahman, she is the supreme Goddess, worthy of worship by the highest; having purified oneself, one should worship that messenger there with flowers such as *śama* and others.
Then the digits (kalās) should be worshipped in sequence upon its limbs by the most excellent practitioners:
namely, the digit of Peace (śānti), the digit of Awakening (bodha), the digit of Pervasion (vyāpti), and the supreme (parā).
The fourth should be known as the digit of the nature of knowledge;
beyond that, another is to be known as Padminī, who is the swan (haṃsa) whose pure radiance has blossomed.
The *haṃsa*? By means of the pair, the lotus indeed [is] *ghalkā*; it is contraction itself, yet expansion through the play of the letters, along with *mātri* and good fortune. || 14 ||
When she attains supreme illumination, she is considered to be the Padminī;
in her body, the sixteen kalās should be worshipped by the best of practitioners.

The digit of consciousness (citkalā), the digit of the manifest (sakalā), the digit of peace (śāntikalā), the digit beyond time and non-time (kālākalā), and the supreme digit (parā) are to be known as the dwellings of the Command (ājñāvāstu), merged within the Supreme Reality.
Furthermore, the Śāntikalā and the others are manifested from the nature of knowledge;
likewise, there are the Virāgatā, the Mokṣakalā, and the Paramātmakalā. (17)
p. 816) Furthermore, four *vidyā-kalās* are to be known within the inner self:
*vidyā*, *santoṣa*, *tṛpti*, and that which illuminates the supreme Brahman. || 18 ||
The supreme self-portion (paramātmakalā) is to be known as merged within the supreme reality;
these sixteen portions are established at the end of the Śrīvidyā.
The sixteen-fold digit, whose nature is Brahman and which possesses sixteen forms,
creates the three worlds through the very essence of the yoga of the Self.
The inner self is renowned as being of the nature of *sattva* and of the nature of *rajas*;
for this very reason, the supreme Śiva is of the nature of *sattva* and of the nature of *rajas*.
The Supreme Self (Paramātman) is to be known as the injunction; it is the essence of knowledge and the achiever of the fourth state (turya).
One should certainly manifest these digits within the supreme body.
Know that her face is indeed the meaning of that word, without a doubt;
then, from the word and its meaning, [one proceeds] in order to the pair of breasts.
Sound is indeed the root of yoga and of the scripture; this is the definitive conclusion.
Sound is undoubtedly the source of all living beings. (24)
There, in the triangle, one should worship Śakti as the garland of the bhaga;
in the center, which consists of universal bliss, one should worship the supreme Sundarī.
Then, the practitioner of mantra should worship Śiva within his own self as the liṅga, as well as Tāra, Bhuvaneśvarī, and Mahātripurasundarī. (26)
Salutation to Śiva; this ten-syllable Vidyā has been proclaimed.
Through their mutual essential nature, it becomes the essence of the bliss of Brahman. (27)
One should visualize that nectar, brought by the mantras through the mind, as having entered via the nostrils;
then, having conjoined it with the nectar of the *arghya* offering, one should worship the Śrīcakra. || 28 ||
The substance produced from the *kuṇḍa* and *golaka* is said to be supremely difficult to obtain;
it exists within the knowledge consisting of the bliss of Brahman, which is devoid of both sin and merit. (29)
A Brāhmaṇa is not truly a Brāhmaṇa, nor is a Kṣattriya truly a Kṣattriya;
a Vaiśya likewise would not be a Vaiśya, and a Śūdra would not even be a Śūdra.
One who is a caṇḍāla is not truly a caṇḍāla, nor is one who is a pukkasa truly a pukkasa;
one should understand all things as equal through the definitive realization of the ultimate truth. 31.
Water fallen from the sky travels by way of the drops;
yet the water situated in the middle of a village is filled with excrement, urine, and the like. (32)
Just as the blood of deer, cows, horses, cats, donkeys, and other such creatures, when all mixed together, flows into the Gaṅgā; || 33 ||
Just as all the water of the Gaṅgā becomes nectar and no turbidity remains,
so too is there equality toward all living beings within the knowledge that consists of pure consciousness.
In all substances, equanimity is constant; there is no doubt about this.
Just as this light of the sun proceeds by means of its very being (sattva), so it is here. || 35 ||
Then, it instantly dispels even its own final darkness,
just as sandalwood dries up milk, urine, and the like, but never mud.
Therefore, the minister who knows how to investigate becomes identical with all things;
at that very moment, the supreme accomplishment (siddhi) should be known as attained through the grace of the venerable Guru. 37.
(p. 818) [Description of the Method for the Sadhana of the Wondrous Trikūṭa] Likewise, I shall proclaim the wondrous sadhana of Trikūṭa as well:
the steadfast one, wearing white garments and adorned with musk and kastūrī, [should practice]. (38)
Adorned with ornaments sparkling with pearls, wearing white garlands, that man remains within a white chamber, observing the vow of celibacy. (39)
One should worship with white flowers and offer a brilliant oblation consisting of milk-rice filled with ghee,
as well as rice mixed with the fruit of immortality (amṛtaphala).
The diligent practitioner should present as an offering to the goddess Vāgīśvarī milk combined with sweetmeats (modakas) and filled with various cakes and foods.
[Therein, the practice of the Vāgbhava-kūṭa:
Or, one should accomplish the syllable of the Vāgbhava through the pure intentions of the mind;
the wise man should recite the Vidyā known as Vāgbhava and meditate upon Vāgīśī. 42.
[The Meditation on Vāgīśī:
White as camphor, radiant and pure, adorned with brilliant ornaments, her hands graced by a rosary of pearls and stainless jewels. 43.
She holds a book and a boon-granting gesture, bestows fearlessness, is weighed down by the burden of her breasts, possesses the luster of a lamp, and takes the form of a thread. || 44 ||
Moving along the path of Brahman by means of the sequence of piercing the *liṅga*,
[one perceives] the divine nectar situated in the *visarga*, which is constant and resembles a stream of milk. (45)
42 | "Called Vāgbhava" means the seed-syllable *ai*. (p.
819) Having drunk the nectar of Kula, one should enter Kula once again;
one should go to Kula once more and establish [the consciousness] at the End of the Twelve. 46.
In the thousand-petalled great lotus is the Vāgbhava [bīja], the full moon;
then, having pierced the Brahma-knot with the stream of the sixty-seventh vowel, || 47 ||
The knower of mantras, having filled the tongue with the form of the Mātṛkā letters, should cause the lambikā to enter the root of the palate by way of the Brahma-path. 48.

And having gone outside, one should contemplate the form of Speech at the tip of the tongue as having the nature of nectar, extending from the root up to the aperture of Brahmā; therefore, that region is the tip of the tongue. || 49 ||
The practitioner of mantra should contemplate the Vāgbhava [seed-syllable], ending in the form of a seed, shaped like a lamp,
upon his two hands, his two feet, and likewise within the three channels.
Having raised the Vāgbhava [syllable] from the foundation (ādhāra), one should lead it to the twelfth [center];
having brought it to the twelfth foundation, one should pierce that knot.
Therefore, having brought it to the tip of the tongue, one should contemplate it as having the brilliance of a lamp.
By reciting this one hundred thousand times, one becomes the remover of all sins oneself. (52)
One becomes a master of speech instantly; even a mute may become a skilled poet.
In an assembly, one becomes a pillar of eloquent speech that paralyzes the opponent in debate. (53)

A conqueror of the prideful assemblies of truly wise men, his splendor unassailable, he was a knower of all the treatises on rhetoric and the meaning of counter-arguments through sound reasoning. (54)
Through the composition of verses, the practitioner becomes a creator of great sayings;
with unimpeded intellect regarding the scripture, he should be known as a lord of speech.
[The Inscription of the Mantra on the Child’s Tongue] One should inscribe it upon the child’s tongue within three days,
using honey and white dūrvā grass, or else with a golden stylus. (56)
The syllable *vāgbhava* is indeed nectar, a peak-mantra (*kūṭa*) that bestows the state of mastery over speech;
he alone is truly wise and illustrious, and he indeed shall not be a fool. (57)
[The fruit of recitation upon the head of a child:
If a wise man places his hand upon the head of even a child and recites this Vāgbhava-kūṭa one hundred and eight times, [he attains the desired result]. (58)
He too composes verses in every way, just like Vākpati;
this indeed has been declared as the essential means for achieving the power of speech (vāgbhava).
[The Sipping of Water (culukapāna):

Then, while remembering the Goddess together with the Mother-letters (mātṛkā) and the Vidyā—which consists of nectar—within the water held in the hollowed palms along with the discus, one should repeat it three times. (60)
Meditating on the Sarasvatī-nāḍī as the tongue in the form of a lamp, one should drink [the water];
by doing so for a year, the fourfold scholarship arises in him upon this earth. (61) [The fruit of drinking from a handful].
Thus, he who, with a pure mind, performs this daily at the time of dawn—
that yogi becomes a knower of truth and certainly a sage. (62)
[The Fruit of Accomplishing Kāmakūṭa] Now I shall explain the accomplishment of the good fortune of Kāmakūṭa. [The Method of Accomplishing Kāmakūṭa]
He is beautiful with red ornaments, wearing red garlands and unguents.
One should properly worship her, who is clothed in red garments and whose essence is the central *kāmakalā*, with various red flowers and other blossoms. (64)
[The Contemplation of Kāmakalā]:
Then, in the midst of the sprouts of passion (madanāṅkura), one should contemplate the form of Kāmakalā, resembling the rising sun and possessing the radiance of a flickering lamp-flame. (65)
She was proceeding along the path of Brahman as far as the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra),
appearing like liquid red lac with the streams of nectar falling from the moon.
Having the form of a bandhūka flower, adorned with beauty as her ornament,
her hands shining with a sugarcane bow, a flower-arrow, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
One should meditate on her who is the very nature of Kāmarāja, as red as the rays of the rising sun, within the Kulapīṭhas; in an instant, a state of intense agitation arises.
One should visualize Kāmakalā in the center of the heart, with a radiance like that of the bandhūka flower;
she is the attractor of the minds of women, especially so. (66)
In the region of the crown of the head, the Kāmakalā pours down a stream of blood;
through its retention and application, she brings the entire world under her control.
[The Explanation of the Application of the Kāmakūṭa] Now I shall describe the application that satisfies the entire world;
by means of the first desire, beginning with Vidarbhya, bring about the end of the god of love. (71)
Then, having formed the *kandarpa-sampuṭa* (the Kandarpa-seal) situated within the corners,
the best of practitioners should fashion that which is known as the *makaradhvaja*.

Having placed it upon a beautiful birch bark leaf, one should write [the mantra] associated with the Fish-bannered God (Kāmadeva) using yellow pigment, agallochum, musk, camphor, saffron, and other such substances. (73)
The practitioner should cause the vital breath (prāṇa), established in the object of attainment, to enter the center of a golden [yantra];
or else, the practitioner should mutter the seed-syllable of desire five thousand times.
One should also diligently accomplish the thousand-rayed root [mantra] either in the center of the navel, or in the heart, or in the region of the face. 75.
Whoever contemplates in their mind the heart-stealing Kāmarāja, which resembles a ruby, shall indeed attain sovereign power. (76)
One should visualize the flame of a lamp from the base up to the navel;
from there, up to the abdomen, it has a luster like that of a ruby.
Among these, one should contemplate the Vāgbhava seed-syllable in the heart and the Kāmarāja syllable in the center of its pericarp, shining with the brilliance of the sun. 78.
Therefore, [his body] up to the circle of the eyebrows has a radiance equal to a ruby;
he is clothed in red garments and stands in a house of lac-dye. (79)
Seated upon a red seat and adorned with red garlands,
with his heart full of supreme bliss and his body rendered as the triple city (tripurī), one should contemplate the lovely Kāmarāja [Kāmadeva] whose form is thus constituted. (80)
[The Sadhana of Śaktikūṭa] Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the sadhana of Śaktikūṭa. || 81 ||
One should meditate upon the supreme body, which endures until the end of creation and dissolution, strengthening itself with flowing streams of nectar and destroying all poison. 82.

Shining with golden radiance, possessing the brilliant luster of a mass of lightning, filled with blossoming lotuses and the crescent moon, she displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. (83)
Having meditated upon her who holds the knowledge-seal (jñānamudrā) and who is the very embodiment of nectar, the practitioner of mantra should remove poison existing in various forms. 84.

One should contemplate the supreme Śaktikūṭa, which gladdens the world and begins with the letter śa and ends with na, located in the heart; and that which begins with the throat and ends with the palate, situated in front. 85.
From the *ādhāra* up to the *brahmarandhra*, and from there back down to the *ādhāra*;
then, from the center, the peak of power (*śaktikūṭa*) shines with a luster like lightning and fire. (86)
One should contemplate a pure ruby between the eyebrows;
from there, extending to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), it holds the fourth state (turīya) like a ruby.
From the thousand-spoked wheel down to the base, one should contemplate the Kula-śakti as having a luster like a ruby;
from there, one should contemplate the Kula-śakti extending up to the aperture of Brahmā (the *brahmarandhra*). (88)
A minister equal to Vainateya (Garuḍa) removes thousands of burdens of poison;
he destroys bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas—of this there is no doubt. (89)
It destroys all quartan fevers and all forms of epilepsy. || 90 ||
[The Fruit of Contemplating Mahātripurasundarī Endowed with the Three Peaks] Now, Mahātripurasundarī, endowed with the three peaks,
when contemplated by the practitioner, swiftly brings the three worlds under her control. 91.
Through the sequential meditation on the red radiance situated in the circles of the navel, heart, and mouth, as clear as a pure ruby, the practitioner [attains this]. 92.
The sovereign power of qualities such as *aṇimā* and the like, as well as good fortune, are produced;
by recollecting that name, the practitioner of mantra becomes beloved by the *yoginīs*. (93)
The wheel of the Mothers resides within his body; through that, he shall become happy.
By means of mantra and meditation, the practitioner of mantra will possess vehicles and wealth—of this there is no doubt. (94)
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the *Śrī-Tattvacintāmaṇi* composed by the venerable Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. || 22 ||
The Twenty-third Chapter:
[An Exposition on the Means for Attaining Longevity through the Mantra of Tripurasundarī]—
How Mahātripurasundarī may be endowed with longevity.
Likewise, I shall now describe that knowledge which is exceedingly difficult to obtain on this earth. || 1 ||
[Description of the specific nature of the Vidyā:

She is the supreme, eternal Kālikā, who speaks at the time of dissolution; she holds a lightning-flash and an eye, possesses a fierce face with a sword and a severed head, and is adorned with a tiger skin. (2)
Wearing red garlands and garments, possessing a terrible form and four arms, she holds a sword, a trident, and a skull-cup, grants boons, and has a sharp nose. || 3 ||
For the sake of accomplishment, one should restore the Goddess to life by means of the "Life-Giver" (Sujīvin) mantra of all vidyās.
[Another form of Vidyā:
She is seated upon a radiant, crimson lotus rising from a sea of red water, atop a young elephant;
with her lotus-like hands she holds a noose, a bow made of sugarcane, a tortoise, a goad, and five arrows.

May the Supreme Goddess, the Power of Life, who bears a skull filled with blood, who is enriched by three eyes and full, swelling breasts, and whose complexion is like the rising sun, be the bestower of auspiciousness upon us. 5.

1 | Regarding the word *mahā*: the construction is as follows—"Just as the Vidyā of Mahātripurasundarī is endowed with life (and is radiant) upon the earth, so shall I now declare that Vidyā which is very difficult to obtain.
[The Explanation of the Dīpanī-vidyā]
One should first recite the syllable Śrīṃ, then Drīṃ and Klīṃ;
thereafter, one should recite Haiṃ Haiṃ Kalahrīṃ Sauḥ Kalahrīṃ.
Klīṃ klīṃ is the seed-syllable beneath that; then the syllable drīṃ, and after that śrīṃ.
This is the illuminating vidyā for all, to be employed in all the cakras.
[Description of the Special Worship of the Image] One should likewise perform the worship upon the image and offer the oblation with a concentrated mind;
one should also worship Anaṅgakusumā and the others in the center of the circle.
Having offered the *svayambhū* flower as well as that which arises from the *kuṇḍa* and *golaka*,
one should worship in the center of the *cakra* with various kinds of musical instruments and flavors.
With sounds of the syllable *huṃ*, camphor, songs, and red sandalwood paste,
and by the offering of human sacrifices and the like, as well as buffaloes, rams, and goats.
Having taken the blood arising from his own heart into a vessel,
he should worship the goddess Tripurā and offer oblations before the fire.
[The Method of Reciting the Jīvanī Mantra on the Goddess’s Right Side] One should perform the recitation of the Jīvanī mantra on the right side of the Goddess;
having offered blood from the *balis*, one should then worship Kālikā. (12)
The wise one should then recite [the mantra] joined with Krodhīśottara, endowed with Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā, followed by Krodhānanta joined together.
6–7 | Regarding "the syllable *Śrīṃ*": he states the illuminating mantra (*dīpanī*) common to all wheels with the words beginning "the syllable *Śrīṃ*.
Thus, the mantra becomes: *Śrīṃ*, *Hrīṃ*, *Klīṃ*, *Haiṃ*, *Haiṃ*, *Kalahrīṃ*, *Sauḥ*, *Kalahrīṃ*, *Klīṃ*, *Klīṃ*, *Hasauḥ*, *Hrīṃ*, *Śrīṃ*.
Furthermore, one should then recite: Pinākī, Susūkṣmā, Krodhī, and Ananta.
And likewise the elemental wind; below that, one should write the Praṇava.
This should be known as the Great Vidyā, endowed with the Great Cakra;
it is the Vidyā that bestows great intelligence and destroys even the most terrible [obstacles]. || 15 ||
She is the Great Knowledge, the Great Desire, seated upon the throne of a great preta;
she is white in form, resides in the moon, is youthful, and wears a garland of bhagas.
She who is of formless nature is declared to be Pāripura-sundarī;
she is the supreme, most excellent Śakti, first stationed at the side.
The second is renowned as Kṣiti; the one following that is Paścimottarā.
And she is the Goddess, the Great Goddess, the beautiful Mahākālī. (18)
The Goddess who sits upon the great lotus-throne, the bestower of great life, by whom the world—including gods, asuras, humans, and others—is pervaded from Mount Meru. (19)
Having brought the image to life, one should sprinkle it with blood;
and one should meditate upon the goddess Sulocanā, the warder-off of all evil beings. (20)
[The fruit of recitation on the seat of the pretas:
He who recites while seated upon the seat of a preta shall obtain the fruit of all desires;
he shall become renowned and famous upon the earth and accomplish even that which is unattainable. 21.
[The Description of the Great Meditation] I shall now proclaim the Great Meditation, which is the supreme embodiment of Śakti—
the Goddess seated upon a blue lotus throne, possessing a radiance equal to that of a blue lotus. (22)
She has four arms and three eyes, is adorned with red garlands, and holds a sword and a trident in her left hands, while a vajra and a goad are in her right hands. (23)
She has a moon disc upon her head and is seated upon a sun disc;
she is clothed in red garments and anointed with red perfumes. (24)
She whose feet are served by the heads of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others;
who possesses the intoxication of youth; who dwells upon a corpse; and who is pressed against the Liṅga. || 25 ||
The supreme practitioner should meditate upon the Great Goddess in such a form. || 26 ||
[The worship of the *cakra* following the worship of Parameśvarī:
Having worshipped Parameśvarī with this *vidyā*, the practitioner of mantra, having then placed his foot upon the *cakra*, should sacrifice to the image of Caṇḍikā. (27)
With the *saṃhāramudrā*, the practitioner, with a steady mind,
should then perform the offering of the *bali* according to the prescribed rule and to the best of his ability.
Having become one whose form is bliss, like the son of Sundarī on this earth. || 28 ||
The goddess Kālī, afflicted by passion, terrifying, surrounded by a fierce host, bearing a black sword, and devouring a flood of blood. (29)

I shall now describe the supreme seed-syllable that effects attraction— the most rare and supreme Goddess Mahātripurasundarī— [the description of the seed-syllable of attraction], the highest seed-syllable which brings about attraction. (30)
The station of Viṣṇu is the seed-syllable of fire (Ra) adorned with the fourth vowel (Ī), transcending sound, the point, and the digit, and joined with the Śakti and the Visarga. || 31 ||
The practitioner should recite: "Summon such-and-such a living being," ending with *dviṭha*.
[Regarding the drawing of the celestial maiden and others within the center of the triangular wheel:
Within the center of the triangular wheel, situated between the syllables *śi* and *ra* (of *śiva*). || 32 ||
She attracts celestial maidens who have the forms of children, as well as divine women, daughters of Nāgas and Gandharvas, and Ṛṣi-maidens who move through the sky. (33)
Having drawn [the image], the illustrious practitioner should meditate upon the auspicious Aruṇā;
having placed Javā and Kanyakā upon his heart, his crown, and his excellent limbs, he should contemplate Satī.
Taking a red flower scented with saffron and perfume,
and having offered a hundred [offerings] in the center of the circle, one should worship by uttering the maiden's name;
that woman, afflicted by the arrow of Māra, will arrive.

[The Description of the Meditation on Cāmuṇḍā] As the root-vidyā of Mahātripurasundarī has been declared, so too is Cāmuṇḍā, whose name is formed by permutation; I shall now describe her meditation, which is difficult to attain. (36)
The young girl resembles ten million suns; she has three eyes, wears crimson garments, holds a bow, a book, and arrows, and is as radiant as a bandhūka flower.
She is seated upon the cakra-linga, her hips adorned with a girdle;
her form is elevated by the weight of her breasts, and her face is filled with vermilion.
Adorned with a network of small bells from the rubies of her shimmering crown,
she is graced with a pearl necklace and beautified by the three folds of skin upon her waist.
The best of practitioners should worship the Goddess—who is enriched with every kind of erotic attire and who causes the onset of passion—with Nityānanda and the other [attendants]. (40)
[The Praise of the Knowledge that is Extremely Difficult to Obtain] This knowledge has been proclaimed; I shall now speak of that which is very difficult to obtain.
(p. 830) It is the goddess renowned in the world as the dweller upon the great mountain.
With his heart full of supreme bliss, he should accomplish that which is of a deluding nature. || 41 ||
She whose bliss pervades the universe, who is the supreme digit of the Goddess, and who bestows great delusion upon gods, asuras, humans, and others. (42)
Then the entire universe, including all mobile and immobile beings, is eternally colored by the Goddess;
the wicked enemy becomes a servant, and the Lord becomes the master of all people. (43)
Now, therefore, I shall fully proclaim this knowledge which is most difficult to attain,
which is conjoined with Śiva and Śakti, and adorned with the fourth vowel.
Endowed with *nāda* and *bindu*, she is the enchantress of all the worlds;
she resides in the center of the wheel within the triangle, between the letters *ra* and *ha*.
The vocative case itself, conjoined with the word denoting the object to be accomplished, is the Śakti, enclosed by the noose and the goad and adorned with the Nāda and Bindu. (46)
[The Explanation of the Prāṇa-mantra:

The seven letters beginning with *ya* and ending with *sa*, joined with the ether (*vyoma*), the *sarga* (visarga), and the moon (*indu*); at the end of that should be the *haṃsa*-mantra, and after that one should utter the word *amuṣya*. (47)
One should say "prāṇāḥ," and then "iha prāṇāḥ" as the next word;
then one should say "amuṣya jīva iha tiṣṭhatu" followed by the name of the person concerned.

47. Regarding the phrase "the seven beginning with *ya*": they are as follows—*yaṃ*, *raṃ*, *laṃ*, *vaṃ*, *śaṃ*, *ṣaṃ*, *saṃ*, *haṃ*, *saḥ*. The Prāṇamantra is: "The vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) of such-and-such a person are here; the life-force (*jīva*) of such-and-such a person is established here; all the senses (*sarvendriyāṇi*) of such-and-such a person, as well as his speech, mind, eyes, ears, nose, and breath (*vāṅmanaścakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇaprāṇāḥ*), having come here, may they remain happily for a long time, Svāhā! Thus is the Prāṇamantra.
All his sense faculties— speech, mind, sight,
hearing, smell, and breath— having come here, shall dwell happily for a long time.
Let this Prāṇamantra, ending with the wife of Vahni (svāhā), be thus declared. || 49 ||
One should employ the [mantras] beginning with *pāśa* at the start of the word *pratyamuṣya*;
in place of the word *amuṣya*, one should utter the name of the person to be acted upon (*sādhya*).
The life-force mantra (prāṇamantra) has been declared by the wise for ritual applications;
one should employ it for the attainment of objectives such as the summoning of established vital breaths. 51.
The best of practitioners should worship all these groups of Vidyās; this is the doctrine proclaimed in the Bṛhacchīkrama Tantra. (52)
[The Description of Wearing the Great Yantra] Now, the supreme wearing of the specific great yantra is being described:
having performed a bath on an auspicious day, at an auspicious moment and under an auspicious planetary conjunction (lagna). || 53 ||
Having performed worship on the great festival day of Siddhiyoga, one should write this.
[The specification of substances for writing the mantra:
The substance produced from the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa*, as well as the *svayaṃbhū* flower; 54.
With these substances—rocanā, saffron, honey, camphor, sandalwood, and musk—one should draw the enchanting King of Wheels (cakrarāja). || 55 ||
[The Method of Writing:
The most excellent practitioner should write the *māyā* (the syllable *hrīṃ*) situated within a triangle;
placed between the letters *ra* and *ha*, it grants the presence of the deities. (56)
One should write the name of the person to be accomplished (sādhya), ending in the accusative case, above that;
right there, one should write the entire Mātṛkā in its sequential order.
[The Method for Purifying the Yantra: One should sprinkle it with the nectar of the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) while reciting the root mantra.
Then, one should recite the Vidyā one hundred and eight times over the installed vital breaths (prāṇas). 58.
Having touched that, the practitioner of mantras, intent on meditation upon the Goddess, should recite the mantra;
[the method of retention: having placed it in the center of gold or again of silver. (59)
By placing [the mantra] on the hand, one obtains mastery; on the heart, a woman becomes very dear;
on the throat, one obtains wealth; on the forehead, there is immobilization and yawning.
One attains liberation by wearing it on the crest; therefore, one should wear it with effort.
It must be worn with diligence and concealed again and again. 61.
[The distinction between worthy and unworthy recipients regarding the bestowal of mantras: One must not give it to one who is insincere, nor even to one's own son or disciple.
