Then, having performed the ritual resolve according to the rules in a well-adorned temple, crowded with banners and flags and beautified by lofty archways; || 67 ||
Adorned with canopies featuring rows of umbrellas, whisks, and garlands,
one should draw a *sarvatobhadra* mandala and likewise install the *kalaśa*.
One should worship one's chosen deity with the sixteen modes of service;
having honored the deities of the limbs, one should sacrifice to the respective hosts of deities.
One should offer one hundred and eight oblations with the mantra to be recited hereafter;
with the ten-syllable mantra, one should present an excellent temple to Durgā.
The great seed-syllable of Bhuvaneśī and the pair of Durgā are proclaimed;
having uttered the three-syllabled Rakṣiṇī, the mantra concludes with the wife of Fire (svāhā). (71)
[The Fruit of Giving a Monastery] Whoever should give a well-established temple with this mantra attains all sovereignty and shall dwell in heaven for ten thousand kalpas. (72)
[The Instruction on the Means of Accomplishment] Here, in this divine and supreme seat (pīṭha), one should accomplish the highest siddhi;
having become self-restrained on the seventh day, one shall conquer Śivā on the great eighth day. 73.
Then, at the junction of time (saṃdhi), one should perform the great bath and the great worship, and offer the bali-oblation;
having placed a lamp upon [the deity's] head, one should worship Śivā with those [same] red flowers.

Having prepared a seat from the body of a goat, the practitioner who has conquered his senses should mentally recite the mantra while meditating upon it with a focused mind; if he remains free from fear, he shall become a king in this world and equal to Śiva in the next world.
[Instruction on the specific results of the practice:
The man who always meditates upon the Goddess as being identical with his own self—of him the entire world, including yakṣas, rākṣasas, and humans, shall become submissive. (76)
Having become one with that through his state of being, whatever he sees with his eye, each such person becomes his servant; and each such woman of noble family goes along with him.
71. Regarding "Bhuvaneśī": by this, the mantra *hrīṃ durge durge rakṣiṇi svāhā* is formed. (p.

879) Having become one with that through meditative absorption (*bhāva*), whomsoever he looks upon while possessed by wrath, that person's fortune is instantly destroyed and they suddenly become miserable. 78.
Having become absorbed in that being through his devotion, whatever he beholds with a serene mind, he is certainly liberated from all sins and becomes like a servant [of that deity]. (79)
Having become absorbed in that state through meditative cultivation, whatever deceased person one contemplates quickly perishes, stripped of fortune along with his servants, forces, and vehicles.
Having become one with that state of being, whatever person the practitioner hates, he becomes hated by everyone in the whole world; of this there is no doubt. || 81 ||
[The Praise of Homa] On one side are all ritual actions, and on the other side is the practice of recitation (*japa*);
the rite of *homa* excels them all—for what is there that cannot be accomplished through *homa*? (82)

[Condemnation of Omitting the Fire Offering: If a practitioner who has been initiated by this [rite] is devoid of the fire offering, he will undoubtedly experience suffering both mentally and physically. (83)
For those who do not perform the Agnihotra, the Great Goddess, having become the fire itself, swiftly devours their wealth, as well as their houses, fields, and cattle. (84)
That which has been acquired with great hardship and accumulated over a long time—
dearer even than one's own life— is swiftly swallowed by the sovereign fire.
[The Praise of the Agnihotra] Without the Agnihotra, one cannot truly become a vessel for prosperity;
however, for one devoted to the Agnihotra in this world, even fire becomes cool. (86)
Even if one is engaged in wealth such as houses, fields, and so forth, that [wealth] will not burn [the practitioner];
for the Goddess of the Gods dwells in fire; therefore, one should always offer oblations into the fire.
One should constantly worship the Guru with the three most excellent kinds of wealth.
Having gathered together with all practitioners, one should always enter the sacred pledge (samaya);
and having abandoned uninitiated twice-born men, one should perform the ritual action.
[The Praise of the Cakra] When the cakra is active, all the castes situated therein are twice-born; when the Bhairavī-cakra has ceased, all the castes are distinct once more. 90.
While the sons of the Goddess remain present, one should not enter into a [sexual] union alone;
for him, inauspiciousness arises and the loss of spiritual accomplishment occurs. (91)
[The Prohibition of Stinginess with Wealth] One should accomplish all rites after abandoning stinginess regarding wealth;
stinginess with wealth quickly destroys one's son, longevity, fame, and fortune. (92)
[The Prohibition Against Deceiving the Guru and the Divine] He who, having deceived his guru and the deity, accumulates wealth,
is led away by kings or else is led away by thieves. (93)
Yakṣas may preside over it, or fire may consume it after a long time;
having abandoned what was buried, one dies, for it is true that one does not enjoy its fruits. 94.
[The praise of offering into the fire and giving to the Guru: An oblation offered into the fire possesses one quality, and a gift given to the Guru possesses one quality;
yet it is obtained multiplied ten millionfold—believe this and do not doubt it. (95)
He who has no trust in anyone yet accumulates wealth will either be taken away by kings or carried off by thieves. (96)
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the *Śrī-Tattvacintāmaṇi* composed by the holy Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. || 26 ||
The *Śrītattvacintāmaṇi* is completed.
